# TENSA: API map for LLM agents

TENSA is a web workbench + HTTP/WebSocket API around the ANDES power-system
simulator. Everything the UI does goes through this API, so an agent can do
everything a human can. No authentication: the server trusts the local user and
binds to 127.0.0.1 by default.

Base URL: http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api  (all routes below are relative to /api)
Full machine-readable contract: GET /openapi.json  (Swagger UI at /docs, ReDoc at /redoc)
Copy-paste examples: examples/ in the repo (curl walkthrough + Python client).
Documentation for people: https://roger-go.github.io/TENSA/ (API guide at /api/, every route at /reference/api/).
Install and start: pip install tensa, then tensa serve --workspace <dir> --port 8000.
GET /api/version and tensa --version say which version is running.

## Golden workflow (order matters)

1. POST /sessions                          → {"session_id": "...", "engine": "andes"}  (one engine per session, isolated
                                             subprocess; optional body {"engine": "andes"} — no body or {} is ANDES;
                                             {"engine": "sienna"} runs Julia/PowerSystems (409 with the reason where
                                             Julia is not set up; the worker's first request waits a minute or two
                                             while Julia starts). A Sienna session reads .raw (+ one .dyr) and .m,
                                             and answers POST /case, POST /reload, GET /topology, GET /keys,
                                             POST /pflow (tolerance and max_iterations only; any other setting is
                                             422) and GET /operating-point; every other session route answers 409
                                             naming the engines that have it. A Sienna session also answers
                                             POST /tds (batch only; tf, optional h and load_model impedance|power|as-case;
                                             integrator, tds_config_overrides, dae_vars and controllers are 422; traces are
                                             named quantity|key, rotor_angle_rel is not reported), POST /tds/init (test_init
                                             false is 422) and POST/GET /sessions/{id}/disturbances (a Fault on a bus, a
                                             Toggle on a Line or on a generator; anything else is 422). A .dyr with records PowerSystems does
                                             not support is refused (422 naming each) unless /case is sent
                                             "on_unsupported": "drop", which loads without them and logs a warning
                                             for each to GET /sessions/{id}/messages)
GET /engines                               → {"engines": [...]}  (every engine the server knows, available or not, each with
                                             available, unavailable_reason, versions, formats read/write, routines, ops,
                                             editing; no session needed)
2. POST /sessions/{id}/case                {"primary_path": "ieee14_full.xlsx"}  primary_path is RELATIVE to the server's --workspace dir (put a file there with POST /workspace/files; a fresh workspace already holds ieee14_full.xlsx, kundur_full.xlsx, wscc9.xlsx, ieee39_full.xlsx and npcc.xlsx; GET /examples lists more); formats: xlsx raw dyr json m; optional "addfiles": ["...dyr"]; optional "on_unsupported": "refuse" | "drop" (Sienna only, ignored by ANDES)
3. (pre-setup only) POST /sessions/{id}/disturbances  (add faults/toggles/alters BEFORE running anything)
4. POST /sessions/{id}/pflow               → converged flag + bus voltages; or POST /sessions/{id}/tds {"tf": 5.0} for time-domain (batch, synchronous)
                                             pflow also returns, per line, P/Q at both ends, the loss and the loading in % of rate_a (null when unrated),
                                             per generator, its Q limits in MVAr, and a "summary" (generation, load, shunts, losses, slack output)
                                             optional body, for that run only: {"tolerance": 1e-6, "max_iterations": 25, "flat_start": false,
                                             "enforce_q_limits": false, "method": "NR", "n_factorize": 4, "linesearch": true}.
                                             method is NR, dishonest (reuses the Jacobian after the first n_factorize iterations) or
                                             NK (Newton-Krylov, SciPy's stopping rule: tolerance, max_iterations and linesearch do not
                                             apply, and iterations is 0); linesearch is the backtracking line search of NR and dishonest.
                                             Q limits are reported, not enforced, unless enforce_q_limits is true or the case
                                             file turns them on; false turns that off. Left-out settings keep the case's own.
                                             "settings" in the response is what the run used. If it did not converge, retry with a higher
                                             max_iterations, flat_start true, or a looser tolerance.
5. GET  /sessions/{id}/operating-point     → PflowResult: bus_voltages/bus_angles dicts (keyed by bus idx),
                                             line_flows, generator_outputs, load_consumption
6. POST /sessions/{id}/reload              → back to pre-setup state (required to add MORE disturbances after a run)
7. DELETE /sessions/{id}                   → cleanup

Key state rule: a session is "pre-setup" after case load / reload, and "setup" after the
first PF/TDS run. Disturbances and topology edits (add/edit/delete elements) are
REJECTED with 409 once setup has happened: the error's "recovery" field tells you to reload.

## Errors

All errors are RFC-7807 ProblemDetails JSON: {type, title, status, detail, recovery}.
"recovery" is machine-actionable: {kind: load-case | reload-case | run-pflow | retry |
add-measurements | wait-for-job | wait-for-sweep | none, label: "..."}. Follow it.

## Route inventory

Sessions:        POST/GET /sessions · GET/DELETE /sessions/{id}
                 (a session with no request for 180 s is reaped; GET /sessions/{id} counts as one;
                 every session descriptor carries "engine")
Engines:         GET /engines  (the engines a session can be created for and what each can do)
                 Sienna needs pip install "tensa[sienna]", Julia 1.13 (on PATH or TENSA_JULIA) and a run of
                 tensa warm-cache --engine sienna, again after a TENSA upgrade; GET /engines' unavailable_reason
                 says which is missing.
Case+topology:   POST /sessions/{id}/case · POST /sessions/{id}/reload · GET /sessions/{id}/topology
                 GET /sessions/{id}/topology/models/{model}/alterable_params · GET /sessions/{id}/connectivity
                 GET /sessions/{id}/ybus  (the bus admittance matrix ANDES builds from lines, transformers and
                 shunts: {n_bus, base_mva, bus_idx, bus_key, entries:[{row, col, re, im}]}, the nonzeros only, per unit
                 on base_mva, row and column i being the bus bus_idx[i] / bus_key[i]; it reflects device status at
                 the time of the call and needs no power flow, but sets the case up, which closes it to disturbances;
                 422 past 500000 nonzeros)
                 GET /sessions/{id}/network-matrix?kind=ptdf|lodf|ybus|incidence  (Sienna only, default ptdf; the
                 matrix PowerNetworkMatrices builds, per unit on base_mva: {kind, n_rows, n_cols, n_entries, complex,
                 base_mva, rows, cols, ref_buses (absent for ybus), distributed_slack (always false), values (row by
                 row, dense kinds) or entries (the nonzeros of ybus as {row, col, re, im})}; each axis entry is an arc
                 {from, to, keys} (the keys of every branch on the arc) or a bus {bus, key}; 422 for an unknown kind
                 or past 250000 entries, 409 on an ANDES session, which has GET /sessions/{id}/ybus)
Keys:            GET /sessions/{id}/keys  (every element's key, each with bucket, model, idx and source, plus
                 "problems"; empty lists when no case is loaded. Every TopologyEntry also carries "key", the
                 topology carries "has_dynamics", and a pflow result carries "keys": per kind (bus, line,
                 generator, load) the stringified idx of each result entry mapped to its key. A key names an
                 element the same way in every engine: bus:7, branch:7-8-1, gen:1-1, gen:1-1/exciter)
Case document:   GET /sessions/{id}/case/neutral  (the loaded case in the engine-neutral form of spec section 5:
                 tensa_case 1, base_mva, freq_hz, source, buses, lines, transformers, generators, loads, shunts,
                 dynamics (key, unit, role, model; values and names null in this version, which "notes" says),
                 events, ext; what the case does not give is null, never an engine default; both engines answer
                 it; 409 when no case has been loaded)
Power flow:      POST /sessions/{id}/pflow · GET /sessions/{id}/operating-point
TDS:             POST /sessions/{id}/tds  (batch; body: tf, optional h, integrator, tds_config_overrides, dae_vars, controllers)
                 integrator: trapezoidal (default, fixed step h) | backeuler (fixed step h, first order) | trap_adapt |
                 qndf (variable step, error control from tds_config_overrides rtol/atol, bounds max_step/min_step; h
                 ignored). Same values in the start_tds frame. qndf after steps taken with another integrator: 422,
                 reload first; the others switch freely. The result echoes "integrator".
                 dae_vars: ANDES variables to record, named as ANDES names them ("omega GENROU 1", "vf GENROU 2");
                 their values at every step come back under "traces" ({t, variables:[{name, values}], truncated}):
                 one row per step ANDES solved, at the time it solved it, the last at tf when the run reached it.
                 GET /sessions/{id}/dae-variables[?q=&kind=&model=&limit=&offset=]  (the names a run can record: q is
                 words that must all appear, kind x=state or y=algebraic; needs no run, does not close the case to disturbances)
                 controllers: frequency loops the run closes on batteries and other distributed generation devices
                 (ESD1, PVD1, EV1, EV2). Parameters only, no code. Each is {"type":"droop","model":"ESD1","idx":1,
                 "gain":MW per Hz,"deadband":Hz,"p_max":MW} or {"type":"ffr","model":"ESD1","idx":1,"power":MW,
                 "trigger_deviation":Hz,"trigger_rocof":Hz/s,"hold":s}, with optional "frequency" ("coi": inertia-weighted
                 machine speed, the default; "bus": the device's own measurement), "period" (s between samples, 0.1),
                 "t_start" (s) and "ramp" (MW/s). Powers in MW, positive discharging. The result's "controllers" has,
                 per controller, first_action_t, released_t (ffr), peak_command, final_command and "trace"
                 ({t, frequency, command, output, soc, truncated}, one entry per sample).
                 GET /sessions/{id}/tds/controllers  (the devices of the loaded case a controller can command, each with
                 "p_limit" in MW and "variables": dae_vars names for its command "Pext", frequency "fHz", current and
                 state of charge; "coi_available" false means only "frequency":"bus" works; needs no run)
                 POST /sessions/{id}/tds/init  (initialise the dynamic models and stop before the first step, to find
                 what does not start from a steady state; body optional {"test_init": true}, false skips ANDES's check
                 for this call only. Returns initialized, test_ok (null when not checked, which does not mean clean;
                 false when a residual reaches TDS.config.tol or is NaN), test_init, n_states, n_algeb, max_residual,
                 nan_residuals, clamped [{model, idx, var, limit_name, limit_val, unconstr}] and residuals [{name,
                 mismatch (null for NaN), equation}], both listed whether or not the test ran, each capped at 500 rows
                 with diagnostics_truncated. A failed test is 200 with test_ok false, and ANDES's tables are in the
                 messages. Runs setup and the power flow first, so like a first run it closes the case to disturbances
                 and edits until a reload; the next POST /tds carries on from it, with the integrator it names (qndf
                 included): with a fixed step the same steps as a run from scratch (trap_adapt and qndf choose other
                 steps before the first event), its traces starting at the first step rather than at 0 s, and
                 converged false when test_ok was false.
                 422 on a case with no dynamic models, a power flow that does not converge, or a System already
                 initialised by this route, a run or an eigenvalue analysis: POST /sessions/{id}/reload first)
                 POST /sessions/{id}/abort  (cooperative abort of a running TDS)
Results:         POST /results/convert  (no session; body {"kind": "pflow"|"tds"|"eig", "engine", "result", optional
                 "versions", "study", "keys", "status"} -> {"document", "skipped", "notes"}: the engine's own result
                 as a neutral results document {"tensa_results": 1, "engine", "study", "status", "series", "tables"},
                 "keys" the session's keys lookup for an ANDES tds result; "skipped" names each column left out and why
                 (a dae_vars raw state is not part of the document yet), "notes" reports a truncated result; 413 over
                 128 MiB, 422 for a result that does not fit its kind or a power flow that did not converge)
                 POST /compare  (no session; body {"reference", "comparison", optional "tolerances"}, two results
                 documents as POST /results/convert answers them -> power flow first (rows per key, "operating_point_differs"
                 when a row is outside its tolerance), then per series the largest and time-weighted RMS difference over
                 the overlap of the time ranges with the swing of the reference, then the eigenvalues matched as modes;
                 differences are comparison minus reference, rad differences wrapped to [-pi, pi); unmatched keys and
                 modes are listed, "not_comparable" holds the pairs that cannot be compared with the reason; 413 over
                 128 MiB, 422 for a document with problems (the detail names the side and each problem) or a unit mismatch)
Response metrics:POST /response-metrics  (no session; body {"series":[{"name","t":[...],"y":[...]}], optional t_start, t_end,
                 settling_band, rocof_window} -> per series: initial, final, peak, nadir, max_deviation, rocof, settling_time,
                 overshoot_pct, damping {ratio, frequency_hz}; not the "traces" object itself, which is 422: build "series" from a batch
                 run's traces as [{"name": v.name, "t": traces.t, "y": v.values} for v in traces.variables])
External results:POST /external-results?source=tsat|psse  (no session; the body IS the .xlsx export's bytes, as in
                 curl --data-binary @out.xlsx ..., not multipart (415); reads the first sheet as ANDES's tsat_to_df /
                 psse_to_df do (a header row, then 6 rows for tsat or 1 for psse skipped, then time and the signals) and
                 answers {source, samples, series:[{name, t, y}]}: the columns in the order the tool wrote them, named
                 "column 1", "column 2", ... because the format carries no names, a value that is not a finite number null,
                 a row whose time is not one left out; feed "series" to POST /response-metrics as it is (64 at a time), or
                 plot it against a run's traces; 413 over 32 MiB, 128 MiB unpacked, 200000 rows, 1024 columns or 1000000
                 cells; 422 for a file that is not an .xlsx export or holds nothing usable)
COMTRADE export: POST /comtrade  (no session; body {"t":[...],"channels":[{"name","values":[...],"unit"}], optional name, station,
                 device, frequency_hz, start_time, trigger_t} -> application/zip holding <name>.cfg and <name>.dat, an
                 IEEE C37.111-1999 record with ASCII data: one analog channel per signal, scaled over its own range, and a
                 time stamp per sample; send a batch run's traces.t as "t" and traces.variables as "channels", as they are; "unit" is
                 optional, null values are written as missing; 413 over 5,000,000 values, channels times samples)
Disturbances:    POST/GET /sessions/{id}/disturbances
  FaultSpec:  {"kind":"fault","bus_idx":"7","tf":1.0,"tc":1.1,"xf":0.05,"rf":0}   (3-phase fault at bus, applied tf→tc seconds)
  ToggleSpec: {"kind":"toggle","model":"Line","dev_idx":"Line_6","t":1.0}          (connect/disconnect a device at t)
  AlterSpec:  {"kind":"alter","model":"PQ","dev_idx":"PQ_1","src":"p0","t":1.0,"method":"*","amount":1.2}
              (change parameter at t; method one of + - * / =; use alterable_params to discover valid src names)
Elements:        GET /topology/schema (every buildable model + typed params) · POST /sessions/{id}/elements (add)
                 PUT /sessions/{id}/elements/{model}/{idx} (edit) · DELETE /sessions/{id}/elements/{model}/{idx}[?cascade=true]
                 (delete any element, one the case file brought included; the file is not written. 422 with "dependents" and
                 "disturbances" when other elements name it or disturbances act on it: delete those first, or send cascade=true to
                 delete them with it. The 200 body is the topology plus "deleted" and "disturbances", what went)
                 POST /sessions/{id}/undo-last-edit · POST /sessions/{id}/redo-edit (take back / put back the last add, edit or delete;
                 the topology's "undo" and "redo" name the edit each would act on, null when there is none; a delete put back takes
                 what it took the first time, and is refused with 422 and the list if anything else has come to depend on the element)
                 POST /sessions/{id}/blank (start empty system) · POST /sessions/{id}/save (write case file; format xlsx, json, raw or m
                 (m is MATPOWER v2: power-flow data only, no dynamics, string bus idxes renumbered, bus area and zone written as zero,
                 the loads and shunts of a bus added up; what it leaves out is logged in GET /sessions/{id}/messages))
Jobs:            GET /sessions/{id}/jobs[?kind=&status=] · GET/DELETE /sessions/{id}/jobs/{job_id}
                 (statuses: pending running done failed cancelled)
Messages:        GET /sessions/{id}/messages[?after=&level=&limit=] · DELETE /sessions/{id}/messages  (what ANDES logged while a command ran:
                 {"messages":[{"seq","time","level","logger","source","text","repeat"}],"first_seq","last_seq","next_after","dropped"};
                 level is info, warning or error, source the command (load_case, run_pflow, run_tds, ...); level=warning returns warnings and
                 errors only; logger tensa.notice marks what the server worked out itself, a generator held at a Q limit or a load turned into an impedance, which ANDES does not log;
                 a message that repeats the newest one is kept once, its repeat count growing; it is then numbered again, so reading on by after returns it with the larger count;
                 paths of the server are not in the text (the workspace is written relative to itself, the home directory as ~, any other absolute path as <path>);
                 pass next_after back as after to read on; a read does not wait for a run in progress)
Clone editing:   POST /sessions/{id}/case/clone (start copy-on-write edit)
                 PUT /sessions/{id}/case/clone/params/{model}/{idx}/{param} (edit one param)
                 POST .../case/clone/undo · .../case/clone/redo · .../case/clone/reset · .../case/clone/save-as
                 GET .../case/clone/diff/{model}/{idx}
Eigenanalysis:   POST /sessions/{id}/eig (optional body {"load_model": "impedance" | "power" | "as-case"}:
                 how loads behave in the analysis; a Sienna session takes all three, default impedance, and its
                 result echoes "load_model" and carries "notes" with the PSID small-signal validation note; an
                 ANDES session takes it left out or "impedance", which is what ANDES does, and refuses the other
                 two with 422) · GET .../eig/modes/{mode_idx}/participation (a Sienna session answers it from its
                 last run_eig) · GET .../eig/state-matrix.mat (ANDES only)
                 POST /sessions/{id}/eig/sweep {"model": "GENROU", "idx": "1", "param": "M", "values": [4, 6, 8]} (root loci data;
                 needs a converged pflow; 1 to 200 finite values, on the base the case file holds the param in) → "points", one per
                 value in order, each {value, eigenvalues: [{real, imag}], damping_ratios, frequencies_hz} (index-aligned), mode_count.
                 Each point is the case with the session's edits and the param at that value, read, set up, solved with the last
                 pflow's settings and analysed afresh: the session's own system is not changed (a pflow can still follow), and a
                 point costs a case load. Eigenvalue order is not comparable across points (match modes yourself for root loci).
                 404 unknown model/idx/param; 422 bad values or a point that fails (the detail names the value)
CPF:             POST /sessions/{id}/cpf · POST /sessions/{id}/cpf/qv  (needs a converged pflow; every setting is for that run only)
                 cpf body, all optional: {"direction": "load", "enforce_q_limits": false, "stop_at": "nose", "step": 0.1, "max_iter": 500,
                 "parameterization": "pseudo_arclength", "tol": 1e-6, "corrector_max_iter": 20, "step_min": 1e-4, "step_max": 0.5}
                 (left out, each of the last five is the case's own; the values shown are ANDES's defaults)
                 direction: load (every load and PV generator in proportion, the default) | load-only (the slack supplies the increase) |
                 gen (PV generators only) | custom, with "load_increase": [{"idx":"PQ_1","p":10,"q":3}] and
                 "generator_increase": [{"idx":2,"p":10}] in MW / MVAr per unit of lambda (the slack cannot be named).
                 With load, load-only and gen, lambda = 1 is twice the base value.
                 step is the first step only: ANDES sizes the rest itself, 0.5 in lambda at most. A custom direction of small increases
                 is therefore a long path (ten times the increases is the same curve at a tenth of the lambda); when done_msg reads
                 "Reached max steps (N)" the run stopped short, and a larger max_iter takes it further.
                 enforce_q_limits true switches a PV or slack generator to PQ at qmin/qmax along the path; solve pflow with
                 enforce_q_limits first, or the answer is 409 when a generator is already past a limit. A generator held at a limit
                 stays held. stop_at full also traces the lower branch back to lambda = 0 (the steps after nose_idx).
                 stop_at also takes a number above 0, a target lambda the run lands on when the curve crosses it (complete true,
                 truncated true: no nose); a target past the nose is never crossed and the run ends at the nose (complete false,
                 done_msg "Nose point at lambda=..., short of the target lambda=...").
                 corrector_max_iter is the Newton iterations per step (at least 2), where max_iter caps the continuation steps;
                 tol is the corrector's tolerance, at most 1e-4. parameterization is the continuation method: pseudo_arclength
                 (ANDES's default) and arclength go round the nose; natural cannot pass it (about twice the points, none past the
                 nose) and is refused with stop_at full. step_min/step_max bound the adaptive step: step_max smaller draws more
                 points, and a step halved below step_min is where the routine calls the nose. step_min above step_max, the
                 request's or the case's, is 422.
                 → lambdas, voltages_per_bus, nose_idx (-1 and truncated true when no nose was reached), max_lam (lambda at the nose),
                 "generators": [{"model","idx","bus","q":[MVAr per step],"q_min","q_max"}], "limit_events":
                 [{"step","lam","model","idx","bus","limit":"qmax|qmin","at_nose","would_release_step"}] (step 0: held by the power flow;
                 at_nose true: the nose is where that generator ran out of reactive power, a limit-induced collapse and not a smooth fold;
                 would_release_step: from that step its voltage is back across the set-point and a real exciter would leave the limit,
                 which ANDES's limiter does not, so the curve from there is the one for a generator pinned at its limit),
                 q_limits_enforced, stop_at, complete (false: a full curve whose lower branch broke off), direction,
                 angles_per_bus (bus voltage angles in radians per step, aligned with voltages_per_bus; empty for QV), and the
                 settings the run used: parameterization, tol, corrector_max_iter, step_min, step_max, stop_at_lambda (null where the
                 case's own setting was kept).
                 cpf/qv body: {"bus_idx": "5", "q_range": 5.0, "enforce_q_limits": false}; same response, lambdas holding Q at the bus and max_lam the largest of them.
State estimation:POST /sessions/{id}/se/measurements/generate · POST /sessions/{id}/se
                 generate body: {"noise_seed": 7} (optional) draws the noise the cached set keeps.
                 se body, every field optional and for that run only: {"algorithm": "wls"|"lav", "tol": 1e-4, "max_iter": 100,
                 "noise_seed": 7}. lav (least absolute value) shrugs off a gross error that pulls wls, but converges slowly: give it
                 a larger max_iter (e.g. 1000) when a measurement is bad, or it answers 422. noise_seed draws this run's noise afresh
                 with that seed and leaves the cached set as it was.
                 → converged, iterations, mismatch (J), residuals, measurement_count, flagged_indices (|r|/sigma > 3), algorithm,
                 settings {tol, max_iter, noise_seed}, chi_squared {passed, J, threshold, dof, confidence} (wls only, 95%; null for lav).
PMU placement:   POST/GET /sessions/{id}/pmu · DELETE /sessions/{id}/pmu/{pmu_idx} · GET .../pmu/{run_id}/export.csv
Profiles:        POST /sessions/{id}/profiles/upload · POST/GET /sessions/{id}/profiles · DELETE /sessions/{id}/profiles/{profile_idx}
Sweeps:          POST /sessions/{id}/sweep (param sweep over disturbance/sim values; per-iteration TDS results)
Snapshots:       POST /sessions/{id}/snapshot · POST .../snapshot/restore · GET .../snapshots · DELETE .../snapshot/{name}
                 (a snapshot keeps the diagram layout: "layout" in the save body, else the one beside the case file;
                 a restore writes it back beside the case and returns it as "layout"; 413 for a "layout" over the layout cap)
Bundles:         POST /sessions/{id}/bundle/export (zip: case+disturbances+params+layout.json) · POST .../bundle/import
                 (export takes "layout" like a snapshot does, 413 over the cap; import writes layout.json beside the case,
                 "layout_restored"; a bundle with no layout that replaces a workspace case of other content removes the
                 layout that was beside it, and says so in "warnings")
Reports:         GET /sessions/{id}/report?routine=pflow|tds|eig  (routine is required; 409 until the session has run it;
                 {"routine", "plain_text", "structured": {"tables": [{title, headers, rows}]}})
Workspace:       GET /workspace/files · GET/PUT /workspace/layout?case_path=<rel>
                 (the layout of a case's diagram, <case>.layout.json, schema_version "2": positions of buses, devices
                 and placed controllers, branch routes ("routing": "auto", "polyline" for a route the UI made, "manual"
                 for one the user drew, which a tidy leaves alone), busbars, label offsets, connections (the faces
                 a device connector attaches by and, where the user drew it, its "bend_points" and "bus"), figure settings
                 ("figure.connector_style": "straight" or "elbow", how the UI draws device connectors; the
                 other entries are what the UI draws a figure of the diagram for a paper with: "monochrome",
                 "line_width", "font" ("sans", "serif" or "mono"), "font_size", "dpi" of a PNG, and a flag for
                 each kind of label, "bus_names", "device_names", "voltages", "angles", "flows", "powers",
                 "chips" and "limit_marks"), and
                 "units": by the idx of a static generator, {"expanded": true} where the UI draws the control
                 chain of that generator (its machine, exciter, governor) out beside its symbol;
                 a device position and a unit carry "bus" and a route "bus1"/"bus2", and are used only for an
                 element on those buses; a version 1 document is accepted and upgraded. Cap 2 MiB, on the request body and on
                 the layout as the server stores it: compact JSON with every field written out, so a field left
                 to its default still counts; 413 over it. POST /sessions/{id}/save and
                 .../case/clone/save-as copy the open case's layout to the new name)
                 POST /workspace/files?name=<file>[&overwrite=true]  (adds a case file; the body IS the file's bytes
                 as in curl --data-binary @ieee14.raw ..., not multipart, which answers 415; 32 MiB; xlsx raw dyr json m;
                 409 if the name exists and overwrite is not true; a <case>.layout.json name is refused, PUT /workspace/layout writes those)
Examples:        GET /examples  → {"examples": [...]}: the catalog of example cases, each with "id", "title", "summary",
                 "category" (dynamic | steady-state), "tags", "size", "analyses" (pf, tds, eig), "default", "provenance" (kind
                 andes | bundled | external, file path, sha256, source URL), "extra_files", "citations" ({role, text, bibtex,
                 doi, url}; role is system, data, software or model: the publication of the system, where the data comes
                 from, the program, or a dynamic model), "licence", "modifications", "caveats", "verification", "links" (for
                 an external entry, which has no file), and for this server "in_workspace", "differs" (the file in the
                 workspace under a bundled case's name is not the one TENSA ships; add with overwrite=true replaces it) and
                 "available"
                 POST /examples/{id}/add[?overwrite=true]  → 201 {"id", "primary", "files": [{name, size_bytes, replaced}],
                 "warnings", "sources_file"}: copies the case into the workspace root (an ANDES case from the ANDES installed
                 on the server), then load "primary" with POST /sessions/{id}/case. 404 for an unknown id or a file the
                 installed ANDES lacks, 409 if a file exists and overwrite is not true (nothing is written), 400 for an
                 external entry. EXAMPLE-SOURCES.md in the workspace root records source, citations and licence of what was added
                 (not a case file, not listed). Cite the case when you use it: the "citations" say how.
Version:         GET /version  → {"tensa": "...", "andes": "..."}  (installed package versions, no session needed)
Models:          GET /sessions/{id}/models  → {"groups": {group: [model, ...]}}  (every model ANDES ships, about a hundred,
                 grouped as ANDES groups them; wider than what the element routes build, which is GET /topology/schema)
                 GET /sessions/{id}/models/{model}/doc  → {"model", "doc"}  (ANDES's own text for `andes doc <model>`,
                 verbatim: plain-text tables of parameters, variables and equations, 78 columns, under 30 kB; 404 for a
                 name not in the list, exact case). Both need a session (ANDES runs in the workers) but no case, and
                 leave the session's System alone; 409 on a session of another engine
Health:          GET /health  → {"status": "ok", "version", "andes_version", "sessions": {"active", "max"},
                 "cache": {"state": ready|unchecked|missing, "warm", "generating"}}  (poll it; no session, never waits for a worker;
                 "cache" is ANDES's generated code: until it is ready, the first case load may take 10 s or more)

## WebSockets (live streaming)

Protocol for all WS endpoints: connect → server sends {"type":"ready"} → client sends its
first command frame. Close codes: 4404 unknown session, 4500 worker error.

WS /api/ws/{session_id}              TDS live stream. Send {"type":"start_tds","tf":5.0}, optionally with
                                     "vars" (groups bus_v gen_state gen_power line_flow load_pq), "dae_vars" (ANDES
                                     variable names, each one more column named as given) and "controllers" (as on
                                     POST /tds; the "done" frame then carries "controllers" without the traces);
                                     server replies {"type":"stream_start",...} (metadata.var_columns
                                     names the columns once) then BINARY Apache Arrow IPC chunks, one
                                     per frame, each with a "t" column and a "v" list column holding
                                     the row's values in var_columns order, then {"type":"done",...}.
                                     A row is a step ANDES solved, at the time it solved it (the rows are
                                     ANDES's own dae.ts); the last is at tf when the run reached it.
                                     With "decimation":"mean" and "max_rate_hz":N a row is the mean of the
                                     steps of each 1/N s, and the last row is still the run's last step.
                                     Reconnect+resume: {"type":"resume","run_id":"...","last_seq":N}.
                                     A client that falls too far behind the run, or resumes past the
                                     ~30 s buffer, gets {"type":"resync",...} and the socket closes;
                                     its "cause" is "client_lagged" or "buffer_evicted" ("reason"
                                     says it in words). The run itself is never slowed by a client.
WS /api/ws/{session_id}/jobs/events  job lifecycle feed: "snapshot" then "job" envelopes per transition.
WS /api/ws/{session_id}/sweep/{id}   sweep progress per iteration.

Prefer batch POST /tds unless you need live data: it returns complete results in one
response and needs no Arrow decoding.

## Gotchas for agents

- Case paths are workspace-relative; absolute paths and ".." are rejected (400).
- A request with a JSON body must send "Content-Type: application/json": the json= argument of
  httpx and requests does, but curl -d and requests' data= do not. Without it the body is not
  parsed and the route answers 422.
- GENROU machines: ANDES uses M (=2H); the add-element endpoint accepts H and converts.
- Exciters/governors link to machines via the "syn" parameter (a SynGen idx).
- A reference to another device ("bus", "gen", "syn") may be sent as "5" or 5: the add and edit routes match it
  to the idx the case holds.
- An add that leaves out a parameter ANDES has no default for ("gen" of a GENROU) is a 422 and adds nothing.
- ESD1 battery: needs "bus", "gen" (a PV or Slack on the same bus, which it takes over when TDS starts; that
  generator's p0 is the power it starts at, negative to charge) and "pqflag" (1 = active power has priority).
  "Sn" defaults to the system base (topology "base_mva"); keep it there: pmx/qmx/qmn/ialim are pu of Sn while the
  set-point and the output are pu of the system base. The state of charge is the dae var "pIG_y ESD1 <idx>"
  (name it in dae_vars); it moves by the delivered MW over En (MWh) each hour. Step the power during a run with
  an Alter on "Pext0" (system-base pu, added to the set-point), or have it follow the frequency with a TDS
  "controllers" entry. Not both on one battery: a controller writes "Pext0" at every sample, so a run with an
  Alter on the same device's "Pext0" is a 422 (an Alter on "pref0" is fine).
- TDS controllers act on distributed generation devices only. A synchronous machine's governor is not a target.
  With a p_max left out a droop is limited to what the device can deliver ("p_limit" of the listing).
- A TDS run that goes on from where the last one stopped (a larger tf) with the same "controllers" keeps their
  state: an ffr that has fired does not fire again. A reload or a restored snapshot starts them afresh, so an ffr
  that fired before the snapshot was taken can fire again in a run that goes on from it.
- Line/Transformer impedances are pu on (Sn, Vn1); the add-element endpoint derives
  Vn1/Vn2 from the connected buses automatically.
- TDS batch endpoint is synchronous with a 300 s server-side cap; for long runs use the WS stream.
- After any run, GET /operating-point reflects the final state (TDS end point, not the initial PF).
- A run that converged can still carry warnings (a device whose initialisation failed, a limit ANDES did not adjust). After an odd
  result, GET /sessions/{id}/messages?level=warning shows what ANDES said about it.
- Snapshots restore by replay (reload the case, re-add the recorded disturbances, setup, PF). The
  ANDES solver-state blob is opt-in on both ends: "include_dill": true on POST .../snapshot writes it
  and "use_dill_optimization": true on POST .../snapshot/restore tries it first.
- model names are ANDES model names: Bus, Line, PQ, PV, Slack, Shunt, GENROU, GENCLS,
  IEEEX1, ESDC2A, EXST1, SEXS, TGOV1, IEEEG1, ESD1, Fault, Toggle, Alter, ...
  GET /api/topology/schema lists every model the builder supports with typed params.

## MCP

An MCP (Model Context Protocol) stdio server ships as an optional extra:
  pip install "tensa[mcp]"          (from a source checkout: pip install -e "./server[mcp]")
  tensa mcp --workspace ~/tensa-cases
It wraps the golden workflow (create_session, load_case, run_pflow, run_tds,
add_disturbance, get_topology, get_operating_point, list_workspace_files, list_examples,
add_example, ...) so MCP
clients (Claude Code, etc.) can drive simulations as native tools.
